name: Strip Sweep
summary: A to-do list where you swipe a row left to shred it into strips, or right to finish it
about: A phone-style task list with real swipe gestures. Drag a row left and it follows your finger with a slight tilt and a rubber-band stretch, while a red bin opens its lid wider the further you go and rattles once you pass the point of no return. Let go and the row is cut into strips that tumble away, the list closes the gap, and an Undo toast puts it back. Swipe right to tick a task off. Good for to-do apps, inboxes and any list with delete.
how: Drag a row to the left: the bin lid opens as you go and the bin rattles when releasing will shred.
Let go past that point (or flick quickly): the row is cut into strips that fall away and the rows below slide up.
Press Undo in the toast within five seconds to bring the row back where it was.
Swipe right, tap the box or press Space to finish a task; keyboard users can press Delete on a focused row, and Up and Down move between rows.
